title: Exposure orchestration checklist and decision guide (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working checklist + decision guide for orchestrating incremental exposure across cross-functional launches (canary-like exposures, A/B cohorts, and progressive feature enabling). Focus is on converging instrumentation, human gating, and automated fallback rules so platform, product, and SRE teams can run releases without ad-hoc firefighting.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: product owners, release engineers, eng-SRE on-call, console team, solutions eng.
- Scope: in-console traffic partitioning and model/route-level exposures for Redwood-hosted API and Dedicated (customer-visible changes handled separately via contract).
- Not in scope: tenant-level legal approvals, billing adjustments, or infra-capacity procurement.

High-level rollout pattern (recommended):
1) Feature branch rollout to test cluster (internal only) — sanity checks.
2) Canary micro-exposure (0.5%–2%) with strict SLI guards for 24–72h.
3) Incremental cohort expansion (2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50%) with automated health gating at each step.
4) Optional A/B experiment where variant B receives different model parameters or routing policy.
5) Full launch after stability window and stakeholder signoff.

Decision tree quick reference (textual):
- Does the change affect model outputs (prompt changes, model weights, decoding params)? -> Treat as output-risk. Start with canary + offline evals.
- Does the change alter request routing / fallback logic (capacity tiers, quantized variant selection)? -> Treat as infra-risk. Start with small traffic and SRE watch.
- Is the change cost-impacting (token/memory/cold-start)? -> Add billing and metric monitors to canary gates.
- If multiple risks: require both product and SRE approval before exposure.

Gating signals (minimum required):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route; compare to baseline (delta threshold: +25% p95 or +100ms absolute triggers immediate rollback).
- Error rate: 5xx+client-side failures; absolute threshold >0.5% for 1h OR 0.1% sustained 6h -> rollback.
- Quality regressions (if applicable): automated eval on representative prompt set — metric: factuality / BLEU-ish / embedding-distance; rollback if metric delta exceeds configured tolerance.
- Resource signals: GPU utilization >85% sustained for 10m OR memory OOM count >0 -> scale down exposure and page infra-owner.
- Cost signals: per-token cost change >20% across cohort -> notify finance + product.

Minimal observability checklist to attach to the rollout: (must all exist before 0.5% canary)
- Live per-cohort dashboards: tokens, requests/s, p50/p95/p99, error rates, tail-kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Eval harness run and summary PDF linked in the release ticket.
- Synthetic probing: a probe job that runs 1 request/second through each cohort and checks response schema + latency.
- Tracing: request traces sampled at 1% for canary; trace must include chosen model variant id and routing policy.
- Alerting: temporary release-level alerts scoped to cohort.

Human-in-loop steps and roles:
- Release owner (product): creates release ticket, lists hypotheses, monitors quality signals, OKs expansion.
- SRE on-call: verifies infra health, approves or aborts expansion if infra signals degrade.
- Console/Observability owner: ensures dashboards and alerting are configured and responsive.
- Solutions/SE (for customer-impacting changes): twinned with release owner for customer communications.

Checklist for canary -> expansion (practical steps):
- Pre-rollout:
  - Create a release ticket (template link: CONFLUENCE-EXPOSURE-SPEC-1023).
  - Attach eval harness output and sample prompts.
  - Bake new model build id and pin config in the release ticket.
  - Create per-cohort metric queries and alert rules (examples below).
  - Schedule an initial 2-hour watch window with SRE and product.
- 0.5% canary:
  - Start cohort; run synthetic probe; confirm traces record variant id.
  - Check latency and error rates 15m, 1h, 6h.
  - Run automated eval at 1h and compare to baseline.
  - If any gate trips, abort and collect traces + logs.
- 2% expansion:
  - If canary stable for configured window, expand to 2% and set new watch window.
  - Run a short A/B test if running parameter experiment (randomized assignment with imbalance correction).
- 10%+ expansions:
  - Require product + SRE verbal + ticket approval before >10%.
  - Add finance notification at 25% if cost increases anticipated.

Sample alert thresholds (example monitors; adapt per-route):
- p95 latency increase: alert if p95_current / p95_baseline > 1.25 for 15m.
- Error spike: alert if 5xx_count > baseline_mean + 5 * baseline_std for 10m.
- Eval drift: alert if embedding_distance_mean > 0.18 vs baseline on sample prompts.

Quick example metric queries (pseudocode):
- Request rate per cohort: SELECT cohort, count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - 15m GROUP BY cohort
- p95 latency: percentile(latency_ms, 95) by cohort in last 1h
- Model variant distribution: count(model_variant) by cohort last 24h

Rollback playbook (when a gate trips):
1) Pause expansion; if severe (errors/latency) immediately revert cohort traffic to default variant.
2) Tag traces and collect top 50 failing traces.
3) Run local replay of recent requests against prior model variant (if available).
4) Convene postmort with SRE, product, and applied-ML to triage; capture fix/mitigation in ticket.
5) Decide on next steps: re-deploy fix to test cluster OR revert permanently for full window.

Open questions for this template (please add inputs during review):
- Exact SLI thresholds per product route — should we maintain a central catalog of baseline SLIs? Proposed: yes, maintained by console team.
- Are synthetic probes sufficient for parity on private/dedicated deployments? Need a replication plan per customer topology.
- Who is the escalation owner for cost surprises during rollouts? Finance? Product? SRE?

Notes / working fragments:
- Idea: include an "exposure intent" stanza in the release ticket that states why exposure is incremental (safety / cost / performance) and what metric would constitute success after 30 days.
- Consider attaching a small canary-bot in Slack that posts cohort health summaries at 15m/1h intervals during watch windows.
- For A/B experiments that change model outputs, include a human-eval sample set and a ramp cap (max 25%) until offline quality is validated.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-EXPOSURE-SPEC-1023 (release ticket template)
- JIRA RINF-2345 (rollout tooling infra spike)
- rollout-lib PR 412 (traffic partition helper)

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with eng-SRE to finalize absolute SLI thresholds (owner: Ethan, due 2024-10-04).
- Prototype Slack canary-bot that posts cohort health (owner: Priya, POC due 2024-10-18).
- Add exportable per-release checklist template to release ticket creation flow (owner: Maya).

Appendix: Release ticket checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Release ticket created and linked to PRs
- [ ] Eval harness attached
- [ ] Cohort metric queries defined
- [ ] Tracing enabled for variant ids
- [ ] Synthetic probe job configured
- [ ] Initial watch window scheduled (names listed)
- [ ] Rollback owner assigned

-- end of working doc --
